content: Central DuPage Hospital, commonly referred to as CDH, is an independent hospital system located throughout DuPage County, Illinois, in the United States. Its main facility is a 361-bed hospital situated in Winfield, Illinois. Additionally, the hospital system includes twenty primary care facilities distributed across the county and four retirement communities. Central DuPage Hospital holds the distinction of being the first hospital in the county to perform open-heart surgery and is currently the second busiest surgical center in the state of Illinois. The Central DuPage Hospital Association was founded in 1958 when residents from Glen Ellyn, Lombard, Wheaton, Warrenville, Winfield, and West Chicago collaborated to restore a sanitarium located on the site of the hospital's current primary facility. Following an extensive renovation project costing millions of dollars, the hospital officially opened on September 16, 1964, with 113 beds and 66 physicians. Significant developments occurred during the 1970s, including the opening of a 120-bed pavilion on December 13, 1970, smaller expansions in 1971 and 1972, and the construction of a five-story, 112-bed patient tower in 1976. In July 2007, Central DuPage Hospital in Winfield, Illinois, announced its plans to enter a joint venture with ProCure Treatment Centers Inc. and Radiation Oncology Consultants, Ltd. This collaboration aimed to introduce advanced cancer treatment technologies to Illinois. Patient treatment at the facility was projected to commence by 2010.
